exposure: gestational age at birth (preterm vs term)
neonatal risk factors for neonatal sepsis
maternal risk factors for neonatal sepsis
cohort: 94 neonates (0-28 days old) admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH), Mymensingh, Bangladesh, from July 2017 to December 2017 with suspected sepsis
finding: The study found that prolonged rupture of membrane >18 hours, vaginal delivery, preterm birth, instrumental resuscitation, prelacteal feeding, and bottle feeding were major perinatal risk factors for neonatal sepsis.
mod_finding: Vaginal route of delivery was found to be a major perinatal risk factor for neonatal sepsis.
